title: AIVTuber Shadow Moderation Evaluation
description: Offline evaluation of a shadow moderation policy against reviewer labels (issue #77). Evidence only: it records how often a recommendation was accepted, overridden or left ambiguous, and it carries no field that could authorize a destructive action, a promotion, or any runtime control. Cases are opaque identifiers and labels; message content is never present.

review_session_id.description: Opaque session identifier. Must not encode a reviewer, a community, or a promotion decision.

authority_effect.description: Evaluation labels are evidence only. They cannot authorize a delete, timeout or ban, a promotion stage, or any runtime control. #77 requires destructive automation to remain gated on calibrated evidence, so a document claiming otherwise is rejected structurally.

contains_private_production_content.description: Checked-in fixtures must be synthetic or public-curated; private production transcripts are never required.

policyIdentity.description: The shadow moderation policy under evaluation. Rates are only comparable within one policy identity, one config fingerprint, one reviewer protocol and one dataset.

reviewer_protocol_version.description: Reviewer instructions version. Two runs scored under different protocols are not comparable.

runtime_profile.description: Runtime profile the samples were collected under. Part of the identity: the same policy and config produce different evidence on different profiles, so records from different profiles are not comparable.

orchestration.description: Bounded-orchestration identity the batch was collected under (#164). Two batches differing only in deadline, sample rate, concurrency, queue capacity or provider-call/budget flags are not comparable even under an identical policy identity.

bounds_fingerprint.description: Stable fingerprint over the orchestration bounds, so two batches can be compared only when they were collected the same way.

identity_hidden_during_review.description: Which policy produced a recommendation is hidden from the reviewer, so the label is not anchored on the model's own confidence.

action.description: Declared in automation-lifecycle order, cheapest and safest first. `human_review` is the escape hatch that keeps `ban` human-approved by default.

category.description: `none` is the protected-benign bucket: criticism, sarcasm, teasing, disagreement and repeated-but-benign messages are not violations, and suppressing one is counted as `benign_suppressed` rather than as an ordinary error.

ambiguity.description: A policy may legitimately allow several outcomes, so ambiguity is a first-class label rather than a bucket lumped in with disagreement.

review.description: One reviewer's label. Disagreement between reviewers is retained, never collapsed into a consensus.

reviewer_id.description: Opaque reviewer identifier used only to preserve disagreement; it must not encode a reviewer performance score.

acceptable_actions.description: Every action this reviewer considered acceptable. Always contains `label`, and holds more than one entry whenever the policy legitimately allows several outcomes.

case.description: One reviewed case. Identifiers and labels only; there is no field that can hold message content.

confidence_micros.description: Policy confidence in micro-units, retained for analysis. Never used as a decision basis and never thresholded here: #77 forbids enabling destructive automation from model confidence alone.

reviews.description: Every review of this case, in submission order. An unreviewed case cannot be scored.

sample_count.description: Reported with every rate so a consumer can see how thin the denominator is. Highly imbalanced moderation data must never be read as a bare accuracy figure.

benign_suppressed_cases.description: Cases labelled benign that the policy recommended suppressing. Counted on its own because benign criticism wrongly suppressed is the harm a recall-only metric hides.

destructive_overridden_cases.description: Destructive recommendations at least one reviewer rejected.

category_counts.description: Recommendation count per category. Every category present, including zeroes, so two reports compare field by field.

metrics.description: Flat #58-shaped metric map: `shadow.moderation.<category>_count`, the outcome counters, and `shadow.moderation.override_rate_pct`.

divergent_cases_truncated.description: True when the retained reference list holds fewer entries than `diverged_cases`. Counts are never truncated, so totals stay honest. Only divergences may be retained: an agreement is not a reviewable reference and must not consume a slot.

diverged_cases.description: Cases where at least one reviewer rejected the recommendation. Never truncated, so totals stay honest.

divergent_cases.description: References to the reviewable divergences, bounded by the producer's case limit. Holds identifiers and labels only, never message content.
